title: Orient Electric Ltd - 541301 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Orient Electric Q1 FY27 revenue grew 23.5% YoY with PAT up 79.7% to INR31.5 crores, though gross margin fell to 29.8% on commodity inflation.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 saw a strong summer-led demand recovery from mid-April, with revenue up 23.5% YoY and ECD revenue up 22.7% to INR669 crores. Gross margin moderated to 29.8% under commodity and labour cost pressure, but EBITDA margin rose 102 bps YoY to 7% as fixed-cost discipline and Project Sanchay savings (INR10 crores) offset the pressure. Management took multiple calibrated price increases across categories, with fans cited at around 15-16% cumulative since December. Management declined to give margin guidance, reiterating only an aspiration of 32-34% gross margin and continued path to double-digit EBITDA margin.

segments.name: ECD (Fans, Appliances)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR669 crores, up 22.7% YoY, with high double-digit fan growth and double-digit appliance growth. BLDC grew 36% YoY and new products were 30% of fan revenue; premium mix reached 36% of domestic fan revenue.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Consumer (B2C) lighting grew high double digits; B2B/C-Loom grew high single digits, with tender business deliberately reduced. Lighting margin declined 40 bps YoY due to a 2-3 week lag in passing on commodity costs. High-value looms share rose to 60%, up 500 bps.

segments.name: Switchgear and Switches
segments.commentary: Both grew at double-digit rates. Management is launching a higher-value MCB subcategory in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Wires
segments.commentary: Grew more than 200% YoY from a small base. Currently house wires only, sold mainly in North and East markets, with cross-sell through the fan dealer network (about 45% of large fan dealers also sell wires).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Grew double digits, led by Africa and SAARC; Middle East was impacted. Hyderabad plant certifications completed over the last 2-3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a 32-34% gross margin, but declined to guide given volatile inflation.
Management is committed to a path to double-digit EBITDA margin; timing depends on inflation. EBITDA margin trend: 5.3% (3 years ago), 6.6%, 6.9%, 8.2% in Q4, 7% in Q1 FY27.
Further Sanchay accruals expected in Q2 FY27 after INR10 crores in Q1.
Long-term aim of a healthy double-digit revenue CAGR; first milestone of INR5,000 crores revenue, with a prior 14-15% CAGR framework.
Marketing spend held at 4.4-4.5% of revenue (5.5% last year on the old basis, per management's comparison).
Management expects employee cost to stay range-bound as a percentage of sales, with automation helping over the long term but not in Q2.
capex_capacity: Ongoing automation of plants and processes to reduce labour cost dependence; benefits expected over the long term rather than in Q2.
Hyderabad plant is a core export base; international certifications completed.
Continued capex on new products, maintenance and capacity enhancement, described as spent as required rather than cut.
New product launches: Aero O2 (oxygen-enriching ceiling fan), Aerosilent (under 50 dB), Ecotech Volt; 3 Red Dot Design awards won.
demand_pricing: Demand: cooling net demand revived from mid-April and stayed robust through May, moderating toward quarter end. Management said Q1 was a balanced sell-in and sell-out quarter with no inventory build-up.

Pricing: fans had 6 price increases from December to June, cumulatively about 15-16%, with about 10% sequential QoQ in fans. Appliances had about 4 increases (high single to double digit). Lighting rose about 10% over 5-6 months. Switchgear rose high double digit. Wires are priced with a 15-day lag to LME.
Competition: management said most leading brands did not take a June price increase, while start-up brands took about half of Orient's increase. Orient says it has priced slightly ahead of peers.
DTM network added about 3,600 retailers in the quarter. E-commerce grew double digits.
Management said Chinese TPW fans are more price-competitive than Indian products; Europe entry is targeted before the next season.

qa_highlights.question: How much of ECD growth came from price increases, and how much more pricing is needed to offset raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was volume plus value across categories, with fans taking about 6 increases from December to June (about 10% sequential in Q1). It said further price action will be calibrated to commodity moves.

qa_highlights.question: Is there trade inventory build-up in Q1, and how do DTM and non-DTM markets compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no inventory build-up and the quarter was secondary-led. Both DTM and MD markets grew healthy double digits with volume growth, and no split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can gross margin recover in Q2 and what margin range is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 32-34% gross margin aspiration but gave no guidance. It said some commodity prices reversed in recent days, Sanchay accruals will continue, and it will act calibrated to inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses fall YoY, and was ad spend cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said marketing spend was flat in value YoY, with a shift from IPL to digital and premium media. Marketing was 4.5% of sales versus 5.5% last year and is planned at 4.4-4.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs keep rising, and is operating leverage exhausted?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost rose 10.7% YoY because of minimum wage increases, but fell to 8.9% of sales from 9.9% a year ago. Management expects it to stay range-bound as a share of sales, with automation as the lever.

qa_highlights.question: What is the lighting margin decline and B2B performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the 40 bps lighting margin decline to a 2-3 week lag in passing on commodity increases. B2C grew high double digits, B2B C-Loom grew high single digits, and tender business was cut deliberately.

risks_watch: Commodity volatility (copper, aluminium, LME-linked wires) and pass-through lag, which compressed gross margin to 29.8%.
Labour cost inflation from minimum wage increases, with employee cost up 10.7% YoY.
Price-led growth may be tested if the industry does not follow Orient's price increases; start-up brands priced below it.
Quarter-end demand moderation and festive-season sentiment; channel inventory normalisation.
Wires scale-up and the switchgear/switch product pipeline, including the higher-value MCB launch in Q2.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, volume growth and EBITDA trajectory, but notably cautious and non-committal on gross margin, which management said cannot be guided given volatile commodity and wage inflation. Management was defensive when asked about the margin outlook and the post-war commodity cycle, which it said is still ongoing.
key_quotes: Despite the challenging environment, Orient Electric delivered a strong performance with a revenue growth of 23.5% year -on-year and continued expansion in profitability.
So to give guidance on the gross margin would be difficult because none of us can predict what could be the inflationary trends on the commodity that could do.
We remain committed to come back closer to a 32% to 34% of gross margin.

growth.why: Management reiterated a long-term 14-15% revenue CAGR framework (3 years) and a INR5,000 crore milestone, but no capacity additions, order book or timing were given; growth backing is pricing (fans up ~15-16% cumulative), demand recovery and new launches, described only in general terms.
